O.outcome_detail: MPSs of chronological age, biological aging, inflammation, BMI, and cognitive performance

cells.quote: First, we found that these MPSs when applied to children showed means, distributions, and associations with chronological age that were in line with MPS applications in adults: Older children had MPSs of older chronological age, higher inflammation, higher BMI, higher cognitive performance, and a faster pace of aging25,26,34.
cells.note: The perspective reports associations from analyses in children and adolescents; no printed effect size is provided.

O.outcome_detail: MPSs indicating advanced biological age, faster pace of aging, higher inflammation, higher BMI, and lower cognitive health

cells.quote: In the Texas Twin Project, we found children from underserved families to have MPSs indicating advanced biological age, a faster pace of aging, higher chronic inflammation, higher BMI, and lower cognitive health26,34,46.
cells.note: The comparison group is implied by the contrast with children from underserved families; no printed effect size is provided.

D.treatment: girls who had experienced their first menses

cells.quote: We did, however, find a somewhat faster pace of aging in girls who had experienced their first menses compared with same-aged girls who had not.
cells.note: This is a reported subgroup association in the Texas Twin Project; no printed effect size is provided.

O.outcome_detail: cross-tissue rank-order stability of pace-of-aging MPSs

cells.quote: Second, the MPS of the pace of biological aging computed in both blood and saliva tissues from the same persons show high cross-tissue rank-order stability25.
cells.note: The study reports high correspondence but prints no effect size.

cells.quote: While the saliva-blood cross-tissue correspondence of these MPSs may be acceptable, the cross-tissue correspondence for those same MPS appears to be lower for cheek samples (i.e., buccal tissue 27).
cells.note: The text compares tissue correspondence; no numerical effect size is printed.
